title: Creating GitHub PR Templates
learning_objectives: Create a GitHub pull request template file in the correct location
Structure a PR template with essential sections and checklist items
Format template markdown so GitHub renders interactive checkboxes
Verify the template auto-populates when opening a new PR
outline: Essential sections: Overview, Changes, How to Test, Checklist
Checklist items: what quality gates matter for Helm (tests pass, docs updated, etc.)
Markdown formatting: headers, lists, code blocks in templates
How GitHub renders the template in the PR creation UI
Hands-on: Create and commit Helm's PR template, then open a PR to verify it

helm_context.feature: PR template for all Helm feature development

criteria: PR template file created in correct location (.github/pull_request_template.md)
Template includes essential sections (Overview, Changes, How to Test, Checklist)
Checklist items render as interactive checkboxes in GitHub
A test PR opened confirms the template auto-populates the description field

professor_constraints: Show the split view: raw markdown in editor vs. rendered template in GitHub UI
Demonstrate how - [ ] syntax becomes an interactive checkbox in GitHub
Keep the template focused — don't over-engineer it for a personal project
Confirm the template works by opening a real (draft or test) PR as the final step
